articles.title: Mandibular Bone Microarchitecture and Cortical Characteristics in Amelogenesis Imperfecta: A Fractal Analysis and Multi-Index Radiomorphometric Study.
articles.abstract: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) is a hereditary enamel disorder that can present with altered dental morphology, while its relationship with mandibular bone structure remains unclear. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate mandibular trabecular pattern and cortical bone morphology in individuals with AI using fractal analysis and radiomorphometric indices on panoramic radiographs. The study included 48 patients with AI and 48 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Fractal dimension (FD) analysis was performed in five mandibular regions. Cortical bone morphology was assessed using the mental index, gonial index, antegonial index, and panoramic mandibular index (PMI), as well as the Klemetti index. Statistical analyses included independent-samples t-tests, mixed-design ANOVA, chi-square tests, and McNemar tests (p < 0.05). FD values in all evaluated regions were significantly lower in the AI group than in the control group (p < 0.05); the mean symphyseal FD value was 1.29 ± 0.07 in the AI group and 1.37 ± 0.06 in the control group (p < 0.001). The mental index, PMI, gonial index, and antegonial index were also significantly lower in the AI group (p < 0.05). For the gonial index, the right-side values were 0.60 ± 0.25 in the AI group and 0.86 ± 0.30 in the control group, whereas the left-side values were 0.65 ± 0.29 and 0.80 ± 0.28, respectively. After Holm adjustment, no significant right-left differences were observed for any quantitative cortical index, and the side × group interaction for the gonial index did not remain significant (adjusted p = 0.054). Klemetti index distributions differed significantly between the groups (p < 0.05). The Klemetti classification showed a discordant pattern, with C2 cortices less frequent in the AI group than in controls despite lower quantitative cortical indices; group differences persisted after adjustment for age, dentition stage, and scanner type. After Holm adjustment across indices, group differences were retained for all four quantitative cortical indices. Individuals with AI showed differences in both trabecular and cortical mandibular bone parameters compared with healthy controls. These findings establish radiographic group differences but do not determine their underlying functional or genetic mechanisms. Panoramic radiographs may provide useful supplementary information for evaluating mandibular bone structure in patients with AI.

articles.title: Harmonizing Fidelity, Utility, and Privacy in Medical Data Synthesis: A Dual Approach via Survival-Aware CVAE and XAI-Guided DDPM.
articles.abstract: Strict data privacy regulations severely constrain the sharing and secondary use of clinical datasets in biomedical research. Generative artificial intelligence offers a viable solution by synthesizing realistic medical data devoid of original patient identifiers and augmenting existing cohorts. This study introduces two distinct modality-specific generative pipelines tailored for medical tabular synthesis and class-aware medical image generation that share a common design principle-the clinically decisive variable (event status or diagnostic class) is an explicit, controlled condition of the generator-and are assessed with a common fidelity-utility-privacy protocol. For tabular synthesis, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) was trained and benchmarked on the METABRIC, GBSG2, and WHAS500 datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the conditional architecture effectively mitigates the event-collapse phenomenon prevalent in conventional VAE frameworks. For class-conditional medical image synthesis, an explainable AI (XAI)-guided Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) was developed and trained on chest X-ray and CT modalities using a stepwise strategy incorporating low-frequency, edge, and density-based anatomical regularizers. The stepwise XAI guidance coupled with anatomy-preserving constraints increased independent class consistency, whereas its effect on downstream classification was modality-dependent. Across five random seeds and six dataset-regime conditions, the CVAE achieved a mean SDV-style quality score of 0.931 ± 0.001 and a Train on Synthetic, Test on Real (TSTR) C-index of 0.739 ± 0.004, with no exact record matches and a mean distance-based membership-inference AUC of 0.555 ± 0.009, i.e., modestly above the 0.5 chance level. Across three seeds, the XAI-guided DDPM reached 98.1 ± 0.1% independent class consistency on chest X-ray and 86.1 ± 2.9% on COVID-CT; however, on COVID-CT its TSTR F1-score (0.639 ± 0.019) was lower than that of the unguided DDPM baseline (0.776 ± 0.017), indicating that the benefit of XAI guidance is contingent upon imaging modality and sample size. Rather than claiming universal superiority, the study contributes explicit event control with a characterized fidelity-privacy trade-off for survival tables and a systematic component analysis of when XAI guidance helps and when it harms image synthesis.

articles.title: An Interpretable Vision-Language Framework for Discriminating Clinically Defined Groups from Segmented Metacarpal X-ray Regions.
articles.abstract: Current osteoporosis screening approaches are still difficult to apply broadly because they often require specialized imaging systems, clinical resources, and additional operational procedures. To overcome these practical limitations, this study establishes a hand X-ray-based framework for discriminating between two clinically defined groups using quantitative analysis of the metacarpal regions, comprising 2100 healthy radiographs and 518 osteoporosis radiographs, collected from China Medical University Hospital. Specifically, this work proposes a vision-language model (VLM)-driven framework that integrates zero-shot prompt engineering and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting to generate interpretable and computable diagnostic formulas based on the quantified anatomical information extracted from segmented metacarpal regions. Using three VLMs, including Gemini 3, GPT-5, and Qwen3-VL-8B, the proposed method analyzes segmented X-ray regions, anatomical definitions, and quantitative metacarpal measurements to suggest several logical diagnostic formulas. With the guidance of the CoT prompt, the model first interprets the segmented images, then identifies the anatomical meaning of each region, and finally generates candidate formulas. This process links the visual characteristics of metacarpal structures with quantitative indices that can be used for classification. The experimental evaluation shows that the best VLM-generated formula, ( o - i ) / i  , achieved an AUC of 0.9344 under threshold-based classification and an accuracy of 87.5% with an AUC of 0.9120 under ANN-based classification. Compared with the manually defined baseline ratio ( o - i ) / m  , this formula demonstrated better classification performance under the same experimental setting. In short, the proposed framework provides a practical blueprint for integrating regional segmentation, anatomical measurement, VLM-based reasoning, and formula-driven classification for discriminating between the two predefined clinical groups.

articles.title: Integrated radiomics-deep learning modeling of hepatic vasculature for enhanced noninvasive prediction of portal hypertension and high-risk gastroesophageal varices.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether CT-derived radiomics and deep learning features can improve non-invasive risk stratification of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk gastroesophageal varices (HRVs) in cirrhotic patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 454 cirrhotic patients from center A and 77 from center B. CSPH labels were available only for patients from center A. Patients in both centers with available endoscopic findings were classified as HRVs or non-HRVs. A dual-path modeling framework integrating radiomics and deep learning-derived features extracted from multiple major hepatic vessels was developed, and was compared with single-path (radiomics-only and deep learning-only), single-vessel, vascular geometric, and clinical-feature-based models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: For CSPH prediction, the dual-path model achieved the highest AUC (0.892 vs. 0.678-0.870 for the other models; P < 0.05 for most comparisons). For HRVs prediction, the proposed model achieved AUCs of 0.790 and 0.782 in the internal and external test set, respectively. The proposed model consistently outperformed the single-path models (0.625-0.648; all P < 0.05), single-vessel models (0.526-0.642; all P < 0.05), the vascular geometric model (0.528; P < 0.01), and the clinical-feature-based models (0.327-0.728; P < 0.001 for the APRI-based model) in the external test set. CONCLUSION: A dual-path model integrating multi-vessel radiomics and deep learning features demonstrates robust predictive performance for CSPH and HRVs in cirrhotic patients. This approach may provide a new non-invasive alternative for risk stratification and clinical management of portal hypertension-related complications.

articles.title: Detection versus grading on prostate MRI: a multi-cohort study of diffusion, perfusion and implications for biparametric protocols.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Prostate MRI is shifting toward biparametric protocols that omit the gadolinium-based dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequence - a decision validated entirely on cancer detection. Whether these protocols preserve the ability to estimate tumor grade, the quantity that drives management, has rarely been tested. Using unsupervised MRI "habitats" as a transferable probe, we asked whether the diagnostic contribution of MRI dissociates between detecting and grading prostate cancer. METHODS: Unsupervised k-means habitats of within-patient-normalized T2 and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), plus semi-quantitative DCE maps where available, were defined on PROSTATEx (training), frozen, and transferred unchanged to Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy (external; 614 MRI targets and 12,809 biopsy cores with per-core Gleason) and QIN-Repeatability (test-retest). Under patient-grouped nested cross-validation we compared habitat, whole-lesion and clinical models, benchmarked habitats against ADC, validated habitat-pathology concordance against these cores, and tested whether the contribution of MRI dissociated between detection and grading. RESULTS: Low-ADC habitats localized clinically significant cancer across the gland (odds ratio up to 3.05; two lowest-ADC habitats captured significant cancer at twice the random-sampling rate) - but did not exceed whole-lesion radiomics or the ADC value itself (area under the curve 0.69 versus 0.69, cross-validated in the external cohort; cores 0.58 versus 0.62). In 107 MRI-detected lesions, ADC no longer separated grade groups (p = 0.79), whereas DCE time-to-peak did, remaining associated with grade after adjustment for ADC, zone and volume (adjusted p = 0.006; likelihood-ratio p = 0.026), although out-of-sample prediction was weak (cross-validated κ 0.05). CONCLUSION: Diffusion localized significant cancer, but mean ADC did not separate grade in detected lesions; perfusion timing was associated with grade, yet predicted it poorly and has not been externally validated. Whether omitting contrast forfeits clinically useful grading information therefore remains an open question, to be tested before contrast-free protocols are adopted where grade estimation matters.

articles.title: Longitudinal quantitative MRI feature analysis in paediatric focal cortical dysplasia: a retrospective longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a common cause of treatment-resistant epilepsy and can be difficult to detect on MRI. Although traditionally considered static, lesion visibility may vary across scans. We assessed whether MELD-derived lesional imaging features differ across serial MRI in histologically confirmed paediatric FCD type II. METHODS: Twenty-one patients with histopathologically confirmed FCD type II underwent paired T1-weighted MRI; 13 also had paired FLAIR imaging. Images were processed using FastSurfer and a modified MELD feature-extraction pipeline. Lesion-mask feature values were compared with anatomically matched contralateral regions, and time-corrected longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were calculated. Blinded qualitative neuroradiological review was available for 20/21 subjects. RESULTS: FCD lesions demonstrated quantitative feature differences from contralateral cortex. In the FLAIR cohort, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were consistently positive across sampled grey and white matter depths and remained significant after false discovery rate correction (mean paired differences 0.607-0.737; all pFDR = 0.009). Protocol-restricted FLAIR sensitivity analyses preserved the direction of effect, although restricted subgroups were underpowered. In T1-weighted MRI, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were positive across grey matter intensity features, greatest at 75% cortical thickness (mean paired difference 0.185, 95% CI 0.060-0.309, p = 0.006), but no T1 feature survived false discovery rate correction. Neuroradiological review identified possible visually appreciable interval change in a minority of cases, with most apparent change attributed to acquisition-related variation or artefact. CONCLUSION: Quantitative MRI-derived FCD features can vary across serial paediatric MRI. These findings demonstrate longitudinal imaging feature variability, most consistently in FLAIR-derived measures, with implications for repeat imaging and machine learning derived lesion detection.

articles.title: Endovascular coiling with Target Tetra® Detachable Coils for small (≤ 5 mm) intracranial aneurysms: a prospective single-center registry study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Coil embolization of small (≤ 5 mm) intracranial aneurysms (IAs) remains technically challenging. The Target Tetra® Detachable Coil (TTDC) features a tetrahedral configuration designed to facilitate stable coil framing and improve packing stability. Therefore, we prospectively evaluated the safety and efficacy of TTDCs for small IAs. METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, single-center registry study, patients with small IAs were enrolled between January 2024 and March 2025. Endovascular coiling was performed using TTDCs comprising ≥ 70% of the total coil volume. Primary outcomes were the immediate angiographic occlusion rate and packing density. Secondary outcomes included device-related events, periprocedural complications, and clinical and radiological outcomes at 6 and 12 months. RESULTS: Ninety-five patients with 99 IAs were enrolled, including 98 unruptured IAs and 1 ruptured IA (72.6% female; mean age, 59.5 ± 10.8 years). The technical success rate was 100%. The mean packing density was 32.2 ± 8.7%, with TTDCs comprising 89.5 ± 11.5% of the total coil volume. Wide-neck aneurysms accounted for 98.0% of cases; stent-assisted coiling was used in 34.3%. Device-related events occurred in 7 coils (2.6% of 271 used coils), including failure to load into the microcatheter (n = 5) and difficult retrieval (n = 2). Immediate complete occlusion was achieved in 72.7% of cases and adequate occlusion in 92.9%. At 6 and 12 months, complete occlusion rates were 93.8% and 89.7%, respectively, with no retreatment required. Complications included 1 intraprocedural rupture without sequelae and 2 symptomatic thromboembolic events, one with persistent morbidity at 12 months. There was no procedure-related mortality. CONCLUSIONS: The favorable occlusion rates and acceptable complication profiles suggest that TTDCs are safe and effective for treating small IAs.

articles.title: Equivalence of anteroposterior and frog-leg lateral radiographs in measuring acetabular index in children.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is one of the most common pediatric musculoskeletal conditions, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 1,000 live births. The acetabular index (AI), measured on anteroposterior (AP) radiographs, is the primary radiographic tool for DDH diagnosis and monitoring. However, its accuracy is critically dependent on pelvic positioning; suboptimal studies frequently require repeat imaging, causing additional radiation exposure for the child. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether frog-leg lateral (FL) radiographs are interchangeable with AP radiographs for AI measurement in children being evaluated for suspected DDH. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Bilateral AP and FL hip radiographs from 100 eligible pediatric patients (aged 6-24 months) were retrospectively evaluated at a single tertiary pediatric center (01/2024-04/2024). Only AP studies meeting strict pelvic positioning criteria (rotation index 0.5-2.0; tilt index 0.9-1.4) were included. Four readers, including three pediatric radiologists and a pediatric orthopedic surgeon, independently measured bilateral AI on each view in two sessions ≥4 weeks apart. Interchangeability was assessed using the Individual Equivalence Index (IEI) with a 3° margin, overall and by DDH status. Reliability was assessed with intra-class correlation coefficients (ICC) and agreement with Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: The √IEI was 2.07°, with a one-sided 95% upper confidence bound of 2.34°, both below the 3° margin. Interchangeability was maintained in patients with and without DDH (upper confidence bounds 2.45° and 2.48°). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of 0.6° (AP minus FL). Intra-reader ICCs ranged from 0.845 to 0.898 across both views. Inter-reader ICC was 0.783 (95% CI, 0.720-0.833) for AP and 0.807 (95% CI, 0.744-0.854) for FL. CONCLUSIONS: AI measurements from FL radiographs are interchangeable with those from AP radiographs. When the AP view is suboptimal in positioning, FL view may be used for AI measurement, potentially eliminating repeat imaging and reducing radiation exposure in this pediatric population.

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated. RESULTS: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001). CONCLUSION: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction in pediatric intussusception: focus on the frond sign and immobility.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultrasonography-guided hydrostatic reduction permits real-time visualization of pediatric intussusception, but the sonographic appearance of the residual intussusceptum at the endpoint of failed reduction has not been well characterized. OBJECTIVE: To characterize ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction and to explore their relationships with operative findings. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 234 pediatric cases treated with ultrasonography-guided hydrostatic reduction between December 2005 and January 2026. Clinical characteristics were compared between successful and failed reductions. In failed cases, intussusception mobility during reduction and final ultrasonographic findings of the irreducible intussusceptum, including the frond sign and trapped fluid, were assessed. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used. RESULTS: Of 234 cases, 216 (92%) were successfully reduced and 18 (8%) failed. Patients in the failed group were younger and had longer symptom duration (P<0.001 and P=0.002, respectively). Among failed cases, 14 (78%) intussusceptions were mobile and 4 (22%) were immobile. Immobility was associated with bowel resection (P=0.01), and both ileocolocolic cases were immobile. The frond sign was present in 13 cases (72%) and was more frequent in mobile than immobile cases (P=0.02). Trapped fluid was present in 14 cases (78%) but was not associated with mobility or operative method. CONCLUSION: Final ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction may help characterize the residual intussusceptum. The frond sign was common, whereas persistent immobility was associated with bowel resection and was observed in both ileocolocolic cases.

articles.title: Short-term Outcomes After Transcatheter Arterial Embolization Using N-butyl Cyanoacrylate or Coils for Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Nationwide Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate short-term clinical outcomes after transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) using n-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) or coils for acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB) in a nationwide Japanese administrative database. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults with LGIB who underwent TAE using NBCA or coils within 1 day of hospitalization between April 2018 and March 2023 were included. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included surgical intervention within 7 days of admission and length of hospital stay (LOS). Multivariable regression was performed with the embolic agent included a priori and additional covariates selected via univariable screening (p < 0.20). Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted in patients with severe LGIB. RESULTS: Overall, 1197 patients (mean age, 74 13 years; 831 men) were included, of whom 207 (17.3%) were treated with NBCA and 990 (82.7%) were treated with coils. The in-hospital mortality rate was 4.6% (NBCA, 3.4%; coils, 4.8%). Surgical intervention was required in 3.7% of patients, and median LOS was 11 days. A higher Charlson comorbidity index, greater red blood cell transfusion units, fresh frozen plasma transfusion, and vasopressor use were independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality. Embolic agent selection was not associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio = 0.54; 95% confidence interval = 0.21-1.19; p = 0.155), surgical intervention (p = 0.637), and LOS (p = 0.243). Consistent findings were obtained in patients with severe LGIB. CONCLUSION: Short-term outcomes did not differ between NBCA and coils. Clinical factors were independently associated with individual short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluating a large language model for radiotherapy patient scheduling under realistic clinical and operational constraints: A feasibility study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiation Therapy (RT) scheduling requires coordination of clinical constraints and operational objectives. Large language models (LLMs) may provide a natural-language interface for generating candidate schedules. PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of using an existing LLM to generate RT patient schedules under clinical and operational constraints through simulation and retrospective clinical comparison. METHODS: A one-year, three-linear-accelerator (LINAC) simulation included 1400 new patients across 12 treatment categories modeled after clinical practice. Structured prompts supplied ChatGPT with patient data, the current schedule state, clinical rules, and scenario-specific objectives. Performance was evaluated across scenarios addressing weekly treatment-time consistency, LINAC continuity, gap-constrained temporal relaxation, and infeasible request handling. LLM-generated schedules were benchmarked against heuristic and CP-SAT schedules under two objective settings. A six-week retrospective comparison evaluated 2043 appointments against a clinical schedule. RESULTS: The LLM-generated schedules satisfied the predefined feasibility rules in all evaluated scenarios. Across scenarios, 98.6%-98.8% of evaluated fractions remained within the preferred treatment-time window. Adding a LINAC-continuity objective reduced the LINAC switch rate from 52.4 ± 2.6% to 9.4 ± 0.6%, and gap-constrained temporal relaxation reduced daily gap to 47.1 ± 8.5 min and Friday gap to 89.2 ± 18.4 min while maintaining low overtime. In infeasible request tests, the framework identified predefined constraint violations and returned interpretable corrective suggestions. The optimization benchmarks also generated feasible schedules, but their results showed strong objective-weight trade-offs. In the retrospective comparison, all computational approaches scheduled the workload without overtime; the LLM strategies reduced mean gap by 50.8%-77.1% and increased time consistency from 86.7% to 99.5%-99.9%. CONCLUSION: Structured LLM-assisted scheduling was feasible in the simulation and retrospective clinical comparison, producing candidate schedules under predefined constraints. The findings support further investigation of LLMs as flexible, human-in-the-loop decision-support tools for translating clinical priorities into feasible candidate schedules.

articles.title: B 1 +   Optimization in the Heart at 7 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: At 7 T, the short RF wavelength in tissue (∼11 cm) causes destructive interference within the chest, leading to  B 1 +   inhomogeneity and posing a critical challenge for cardiac MRI and MRS. While subject-specific parallel-transmit (pTx) optimization can mitigate this, it requires calibration scans and offline computation. To simplify this process, a static "global" shim was calculated and demonstrated to outperform the default transmit configuration without participant-specific calibration. METHODS: B 1 +   maps were acquired in 12 healthy volunteers at 7 T using an 8-channel 1H torso coil. "Personal" phase-only shims were calculated per subject by minimizing a cost function of  B 1 +   homogeneity and efficiency. The "global" shim was calculated by optimizing performance across the cohort, then validated in six additional volunteers by comparing performance against the native mode. RESULTS: In the validation cohort, the "global" significantly outperformed the native shim. It increased the Mean Transmit Sensitivity by ∼20% and reduced CoV by ∼ 16 %  in the septum. The fixed global shim performance was within 3% of the computationally expensive personal shim for all metrics. CONCLUSION: A fixed, population-derived, global phase shim provides a practical, calibration-free approach for improving cardiac  B 1 +   performance at 7 T. The present results extend previous universal RF-shimming work through prospective evaluation in an independent validation cohort and demonstrate that much of the benefit of personal shimming can be retained without participant-specific optimization. The resulting fixed-phase configuration could also provide a practical route towards implementation on single-transmit hardware for cardiac imaging and spectroscopic applications.

articles.title: GC-ResNet: Interference-Resistant Fine-Grained Classification and Robustness Analysis of Highly Similar Anatomical Structures in Nasal Endoscopy.
articles.abstract: Accurate recognition of anatomical structures in nasal endoscopic images is challenging because of high inter-class morphological similarity and common imaging interference, including specular reflections, bubbles, blur, and abnormal exposure. To address these issues, we present GC-ResNet, an improved ResNet-34 framework for fine-grained nasal endoscopic image classification. GC-ResNet integrates squeeze-and-excitation (SE) modules into residual blocks to adaptively recalibrate channel responses and introduces a bottleneck-style global feature refinement module after the final residual stage to refine high-level contextual representations. Experiments on 6706 unique nasal endoscopic images from eight view categories use a fixed image-level split with separate training, validation, and test sets. Across five training seeds, GC-ResNet achieves a test accuracy of 95.58% ± 0.40% and a weighted F1-score of 95.59% ± 0.39% (mean ± standard deviation), maintaining competitive clean-image performance among the compared models. Stress tests suggest improved accuracy retention relative to ResNet-34 under selected synthetic specular-reflection and bubble-interference conditions, with unadjusted paired 95% confidence intervals for the accuracy differences excluding zero. These results support the potential of GC-ResNet for robust fine-grained recognition in nasal endoscopic images.

articles.title: Prediction of Postoperative Neurological Function Recovery in Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy Using MRI-based Delta-Radiomics Combined with Interpretable Machine Learning Model.
articles.abstract: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) presents progressive neurological deterioration and highly variable postoperative outcomes, while existing prognostic assessment methods have inherent limitations. This dual-center study developed an interpretable MRI-based delta-radiomics model for individualized CSM postoperative prognosis evaluation. A total of 237 CSM patients from Center 1 and 96 patients from Center 2 who underwent decompression surgery were retrospectively enrolled. The Center 1 cohort was stratified by clinical outcomes and randomly divided into training (n = 165) and internal testing (n = 72) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio, while the Center 2 cohort served as an independent external validation set (n = 96). Radiomic features were extracted from pre- and postoperative T2WI MRI images, and delta-radiomic features were calculated. LASSO regression and spearman correlation analysis were applied to screen core radiomic features, and clinical-routine imaging features. Three prediction models were constructed via five machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, and pairwise comparisons performed via the DeLong and McNemar tests. Calibration curves and radar charts were generated to determine the optimal algorithm for each model. Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis were performed to assess clinical benefit and model interpretability. Baseline data were well balanced. 16 preoperative radiomic features, 15 delta-radiomic features, and 5 clinical-routine imaging features were finally selected. The XGBoost-based delta-radiomic model achieved the highest numerical AUCs in the internal test (0.899) and external validation (0.802) sets, demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in AUC compared to both the preoperative radiomic model and the clinical-routine imaging model. The model maintained a balanced performance profile across cohorts. This model maintained a higher clinical net benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified wavelet-domain texture features as risk factors for poor prognosis, while gradient-domain kurtosis features showed bidirectional regulatory effects. Overall, the MRI-based delta-radiomic model effectively predicts long-term neurological recovery in CSM patients. The delta-radiomic model exhibits a more balanced performance profile and statistically better generalizability. By utilizing routine short-term postoperative MRI (within 7 days), this interpretable model holds promise as an objective tool for early prediction of 12-month postoperative neurological recovery.

articles.title: Beyond Model Stochasticity: External Randomness for Diffusion-Based Unsupervised MRI Anomaly Detection.
articles.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) in MRI aims to identify abnormal regions through a model trained on normal MR images. Recently, reconstruction-based methods leveraging denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) as base generative models (GMs) have gained attention. These approaches typically compute an anomaly score by measuring the difference between a query image and a single reconstructed counterpart (or low-diversity counterparts). However, these approaches typically struggle to differentiate erroneous reconstructions of normal regions from actual abnormalities. To address this problem, we propose a novel approach that enhances anomaly detection by leveraging statistical discrepancy from high-diversity reconstructions. We employ image inpainting with randomly sampled masks to generate diversified reconstructions. We can produce diverse reconstructions through image inpainting even when the input masks differ only slightly, depending on the information retained in the unmasked regions. By sampling multiple random input masks, we can obtain a diverse set of reconstructions, enabling more reliable distinction between normal and abnormal regions. In abnormal lesions, large discrepancies consistently appear across reconstructions, whereas normal regions exhibit irregular and less pronounced differences. Since existing anomaly definitions often fail to adequately capture statistical discrepancy in inpainted images, we introduce a new anomaly score. We define a pixel-wise anomaly score as the average of the normalized differences between the query image and the inpainted images generated from randomly sampled masks covering the pixel. Experimental results demonstrate that our method, with its reconstruction diversification strategy and novel anomaly score, substantially outperforms existing reconstruction-based approaches.

articles.title: LIVSEG: A Cloud-GPU Web Application for Automated Future Liver Remnant Estimation.
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of the future liver remnant (FLR) is essential for planning hepatectomy and portal vein embolization (PVE), yet conventional calculation relies on manual segmentation that is time-intensive and dependent on specialized workstations. Thus, LIVSEG was developed as a single-page web application that streams DICOM or NIfTI imaging to a cloud GPU running TotalSegmentator nnU-Net models for automated Couinaud-segment and hepatic-lesion segmentation, with an integrated editor for human review. In a cohort of 60 patients (38 living liver donors, 22 PVE patients; 82 scans), the absolute difference between automated and manual FLR was 3.24 ± 2.69 percentage points (pp) in donors and 4.49 ± 5.14 pp across PVE scans, and the two methods were statistically equivalent within a ± 5 pp margin in all cohorts. Using institutional FLR thresholds, LIVSEG and manual volumetry yielded concordant classifications in 79 of 82 scans (96.3%). Inference was completed in two minutes per case at a GPU cost of $0.014-0.026 per study. LIVSEG allows models to reach clinical workflows while retaining human oversight.

articles.title: VCon-Net: A Cerebral Artery Segmentation Network with Enhanced Topological Connectivity.
articles.abstract: Precise segmentation of cerebral artery from computed tomography angiography serves as a fundamental prerequisite for the clinical evaluation and morphological analysis of cerebrovascular diseases, particularly stroke. However, oversegmentation and undersegmentation routinely compromise topological connectivity and accuracy. This study aims to develop a novel deep learning network to mitigate these challenges, enhancing topological connectivity and accuracy. To enforce topological connectivity, we propose a novel skeleton points distance loss that combines skeleton points with a 3D Euclidean distance field to penalize oversegmentation and undersegmentation via interskeleton point distance constraints. Built upon the U-Net architecture, VCon-Net integrates an axialdynamic convolution module and a multiattention mechanism to enhance the perception of slender arteries and capture spatial-channel-temporal features. A total of 202 cases were included in this study, with 141 cases utilized for model development, 35 for independent testing and performance evaluation, and the remaining 26 analyzed as special clinical cases. On the independent test set, VCon-Net achieved a Dice of 0.8552, a Jaccard of 0.7513, a precision of 0.8568, a sensitivity of 0.8645, with HD95 reduced to 3.16 mm, and β0 error reduced to 2.85. Compared with existing segmentation methods, the proposed framework yields favorable performance. VCon-Net achieves cerebral artery segmentation with enhanced topological connectivity, providing a reliable morphological foundation, which offers an essential morphology basis for downstream clinical evaluations.

articles.title: PanPrompt3D: A Prompt-Guided SAM-Based Framework for 3D Pancreatic Segmentation Across Multi-Sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Accurate three-dimensional pancreatic segmentation is important for pancreatic assessment, treatment planning, and quantitative follow-up. However, most existing segmentation methods have been developed primarily for computed tomography, and their performance across clinically used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences remains less well characterized. We propose PanPrompt3D, a prompt-guided 3D segmentation framework adapted from SAM-Med3D for pancreatic MRI. PanPrompt3D combines a hybrid Transformer-CNN encoder, 3D triplet attention, volumetric prompt encoding, a 3D mask decoder, and a volume-aware hybrid loss incorporating explicit volumetric consistency. The model was evaluated on public T1-weighted (T1W) and T2-weighted (T2W) MRI data and an in-house cohort of 285 water-sequence examinations. With five-point prompts, PanPrompt3D achieved Dice scores of 81.66%, 85.03%, and 85.07% on water-sequence, T1W, and T2W MRI, respectively. Compared with SAM-Med3D under the same prompting protocol, paired Dice improvements were 4.70, 5.80, and 4.99 percentage points, respectively, with all three comparisons remaining statistically significant after Holm correction. PanPrompt3D also achieved R2 values above 0.9 between predicted and reference pancreatic volumes. Leave-one-sequence-out experiments showed reduced performance on unseen sequences, while external validation on CrossPan and AMOS demonstrated transfer to independent public MRI data, with a clear performance decrease on the unseen out-of-phase contrast. These findings support PanPrompt3D as a practical prompt-guided framework for multi-sequence pancreatic MRI segmentation while highlighting the remaining challenge of generalization to unseen contrasts.

articles.title: VISION-GAN: Mask Conditioned U-Net GAN with Multi-Scale Auxiliary Supervision for Retinal Fundus Image Generation.
articles.abstract: Retinal fundus imaging is essential for early detection of ocular and systemic disease, but training deep models is limited by data scarcity, privacy constraints, and class imbalance. Existing generative approaches mainly target global realism, with limited control over fine-grained retinal anatomy and lesion patterns. We address this by explicitly conditioning fundus image synthesis on retinal structural and lesion-specific priors. A multi-scale residual attention U-Net segments the blood vessels, optic disc, and exudates, and together with diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity labels are used as conditioning inputs to a mask-guided conditional GAN, effectively coupling discriminative segmentation with generative synthesis. The generator is a U-Net with a multi-path encoder and normalization-based conditioning (SPADE, AdaIN, and FiLM) in the decoder, enabling structural guidance, appearance variation, and disease-aware modulation, while a projection-based discriminator enforces local and global realism. The model is trained with a composite objective that combines hinge adversarial loss with multi-scale region-aware reconstruction and perceptual losses. We evaluate the framework on the APTOS, EyePACS, and Messidor-2 datasets using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Kernel Inception Distance (KID), Inception Score (IS), Structural Similarity (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR). The proposed method achieves low FID, KID, and high SSIM, PSNR on all three datasets and improves the metrics over prior GAN-based fundus synthesis methods on Messidor-2. The downstream classification study performed showed that augmenting APTOS dataset with synthetic images improved ResNet-18 DR grading performance. These results show that anatomically conditioned synthesis from multi-mask priors yields realistic, diverse fundus images that are useful for mitigating data limitations in clinical deep learning.

articles.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Tympanic Membrane Otoscopy Classification: A Patient-Level, Multi-Seed Comparison of CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures.
articles.abstract: Otoscopic assessment of the tympanic membrane relies heavily on the clinician's experience and therefore exhibits inter-observer variability. We compared convolutional neural network (CNN) and Vision Transformer architectures for classifying otoscopic images into five classes (acute otitis, cerumen impaction, normal, perforation and serous otitis) within a patient-level, multi-seed, leakage-resistant evaluation framework. The study included 2534 otoscopic images obtained from 735 patients. A held-out test set of 148 patients (20%) was not used at any stage of model development and was accessed only once, at the end of the study. For the remaining patients, patient-level five-fold cross-validation was repeated with five seeds, yielding 25 evaluations per model. Seven architectures were trained under an identical protocol and compared using the Friedman test with post-hoc Nemenyi analysis and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Swin-T achieved the highest performance (F1-macro 0.900; 95% confidence interval 0.890-0.910), and the models differed significantly (Friedman p < 10⁻9). This superiority stemmed more from design choices than from the architectural family. The hierarchical ConvNeXt-T (CNN) was statistically equivalent to Swin-T, whereas, under the common protocol, the flat-patch ViT-B/16 ranked among the weakest and most costly models. The difference between the families was small (0.881 for CNN versus 0.887 for Transformer). Temperature scaling, learnt on the validation set, reduced the mean expected calibration error (ECE) from 0.077 to 0.043. Most errors occurred between the visually similar acute otitis and serous otitis classes. Explanation faithfulness was quantified using Deletion and Insertion area under the curve (AUC) metrics. Held-out performance was consistent with cross-validation (difference ≤ 0.043), indicating that the models did not overfit. Hierarchical and locally windowed architectures achieved the best balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. The main limitation of the study is that the data are single-centre and external validation has not yet been carried out.

articles.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Retrospective Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC): Application to Multi-Gradient-Recalled Echo Quantitative MRI.
articles.abstract: Multi-echo gradient-recalled-echo (mGRE) MRI supports quantitative neuroimaging by enabling voxel-wise T2*/R2*/R2t* mapping for quantitative assessment of tissue damage and magnetic susceptibility imaging. Subject motion degrades these acquisitions by introducing inconsistencies due to phase-encoding steps collected at different head positions. Although the gradient echoes associated with a given phase-encoding line are acquired at practically the same head position, differences in contrast, signal-to-noise ratio, and B0 field-dependent phase evolution cause the resulting artifacts to appear differently across echoes and can bias downstream parametric maps. Existing learning-based retrospective correction approaches often discard complex phase information, treat multiple gradient-recalled echoes independently, and apply correction indiscriminately to both motion-corrupted and clean data. We propose Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC), a retrospective image-domain pipeline that couples a complex-input volume-level Multi-Echo Motion Detection (ME-MoD) model and a complex-valued Multi-Echo Motion Corrector (ME-MoC) in an iterative detect-correct-re-evaluate loop, where correction is invoked only on volumes flagged as motion corrupted. ME-MoD reweights each echo with a phase-preserving paired complex gate, followed by a shared residual slice encoder, and a selected volume-level aggregator. ME-MoC is a fully complex-valued, factorized U-Net with echo-axis multi-head self-attention at the bottleneck, trained with a T2*-consistency physics loss. ME-MoD attained an AUC of 0.95 and sensitivity of 0.91 on the held-out detection set. At the cohort-level analysis, ME-MoC improved downstream R2* fitting results relative to the motion-corrupted input and 2D U-Net and achieved the lowest numerical R2* root-mean-square error (RMSE) among the evaluated methods, including modest numerical improvement over baseline.

articles.title: Pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL): a practical clinical guide to contrast-free cerebral perfusion imaging in stroke and steno-occlusive disease.
articles.abstract: The past decade has witnessed the emergence of multiple arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based imaging techniques, with growing evidence supporting their utility across diverse neurological diseases. ASL represents a paradigm shift in perfusion imaging as a noninvasive, contrast-free MRI technique that provides both cerebral perfusion quantification and detection of arterial stenosis or occlusion, offering diagnostic capabilities comparable to the established dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) technique while avoiding contrast-related risks. This review article provides a focused clinically oriented overview of Pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) technique in stroke imaging, discusses the fundamental physical principles of arterial spin labeling, examines various acquisition and optimization strategies, and evaluates clinical applications with primary emphasis on acute ischemic stroke and steno-occlusive cerebrovascular disease, the predominant risk factor for recurrent stroke.

articles.title: Ultra-High-Field (7T) knee MRI: review of technical considerations and current evidence, with experience from an institutional clinical series.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultra-high-field, 7 Tesla (T) MRI provides higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and enables high-resolution 3D and quantitative imaging. Its role in musculoskeletal (MSK) knee imaging is emerging but not yet standardized. PURPOSE: To review current 7 T knee MRI techniques and evidence, detail key technical/physics considerations, and to report a single-center clinical experience through a descriptive study. METHODS: Up to date narrative synthesis of the literature organized by qualitative (morphologic) and quantitative applications, complemented by experience from a retrospective single-center series of consecutive 7 T knee examinations. RESULTS: Literature shows that 7 T imaging can improve conspicuity of cartilage, meniscus, ligaments, and bone microarchitecture with isotropic 3D acquisitions; quantitative methods (T2/T2*, Ultrashort Echo Time (UTE), Glycosaminoglycan Chemical Exchange Saturation Transfer (gagCEST), 23Na, T1rho) show promise but require rigorous B0/B1 correction and Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) management. Our experience demonstrated that 7 T imaging was clinically feasible and well tolerated in a cohort of 131 patients (mean age 33.8 ± 10.5 years ranging from 16 to 63 years) and provided a potential and a subjective increase in diagnosis confidence in selected scenarios, particularly in postoperative meniscus assessment and conservative ACL follow-up. CONCLUSION: 7 T knee MRI is feasible and potentially impactful in specific indications; however, stronger comparative data, protocol harmonization, and quantitative validation are needed.

Preoperative prediction of HER2 status in breast cancer using multiparametric MRI deep learning and clinical features.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: HER2 status is an important biomarker in breast cancer, but its assessment primarily relies on core needle biopsy and pathological examination. Therefore, noninvasive preoperative prediction of HER2 status has important clinical value. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of models integrating multiparametric MRI deep learning, radiomics, and clinical features for preoperative HER2 status prediction in breast cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 257 patients with pathologically confirmed breast cancer were retrospectively enrolled, including 98 HER2-positive and 159 HER2-negative patients. All patients underwent preoperative T1WI, T2WI, DWI, and DCE-MRI. Patients were randomly divided at the patient level into training (n = 174) and internal test (n = 83) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Cli, Rad, and DL models were constructed based on clinical, radiomics, and deep learning features, respectively, along with single-sequence fusion models. Subsequently, an mpMRI model integrating radiomics and deep learning features from all four MRI sequences and an mpMRI_Cli model further incorporating statistically significant preoperative clinical features were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1 score, Brier score, decision curve analysis, calibration curves, and confusion matrices. DeLong's test was used to compare AUCs between models. RESULTS: In the internal test cohort, the AUCs of the T1WI, T2WI, DWI, and DCE-MRI models were 0.666, 0.689, 0.710, and 0.728, respectively. The AUCs of the Cli, Rad, and DL models were 0.571, 0.764, and 0.791, respectively. The mpMRI model achieved an AUC of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.837-0.966), with an accuracy of 0.831, sensitivity of 0.742, and specificity of 0.885. The mpMRI_Cli model achieved an AUC of 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.972), with an accuracy of 0.819, sensitivity of 0.839, specificity of 0.808, and Brier score of 0.122. Although the mpMRI_Cli model had a higher AUC than the mpMRI model, the difference was not statistically significant after Holm correction (P = 0.744). CONCLUSION: Integrating multiparametric MRI radiomics and deep learning features improved preoperative prediction of HER2 status in breast cancer. Further incorporation of clinical features increased the AUC and sensitivity and reduced the Brier score, although the improvement in AUC was not statistically significant. Both models show potential for noninvasive preoperative HER2 prediction, but further validation in independent external and multicenter cohorts is warranted.

articles.title: Interreader and intrareader agreement of qualitative cine four-dimensional computed tomography interpretation for dynamic carpal instability.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the interreader and intrareader agreement of qualitative cine four-dimensional computed tomography (4D CT) interpretation for dynamic carpal instability separately for the binary judgment of whether instability is present and for the assignment of an instability phenotype. METHODS: In this retrospective reader-agreement study, 50 wrists from 50 patients who were consecutively screened and imaged for clinically suspected carpal instability were read independently by three blinded musculoskeletal radiologists in 2 rounds separated by a 4- to 6-week washout with re-randomized case order and identifiers, giving 300 evaluations. The readers reviewed anonymized flexion-extension and radioulnar-deviation cine sequences using a common written guide and evaluation form that standardized the observations and reporting structure; quantitative thresholds for abnormal motion were not specified. The principal analysis focused on round-1 three-reader agreement for the binary overall judgment, estimated with Fleiss kappa (κ); 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were obtained by wrist-level bootstrap resampling (100,000 replicates, fixed seed). Supporting analyses included the Gwet first-order agreement coefficient (AC1), pairwise and intrareader Cohen κ, and replication in round 2. Phenotype, severity and sequence-specific agreement, reader descriptors, and clinical correlation were exploratory. RESULTS: Round-1 Fleiss κ for the binary judgment was 0.679 (95% CI, 0.509-0.830), with identical judgments by all three readers in 38 of 50 wrists (76.0%); Gwet AC1 was 0.681 (95% CI, 0.521-0.840). Intrareader Cohen κ ranged from 0.755 to 0.801. Agreement for the six-category phenotype was 0.529 (95% CI, 0.382-0.664). Among the 21 wrists judged positive by all three readers, all three assigned the same phenotype category in 11 and the same named carpal compartment in 8; Fleiss κ restricted to these wrists was 0.473 (95% CI, 0.204-0.690). Diagnostic accuracy was not evaluated. CONCLUSION: Among three experienced musculoskeletal radiologists, qualitative cine 4D CT yielded an interreader κ of 0.679 for the binary judgment of dynamic carpal instability. Assignment of a specific phenotype was less consistent, with interpretation limited by overlapping qualitative categories. These findings describe agreement under the study reading conditions; they do not establish diagnostic accuracy or clinical validity. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The three experienced readers showed agreement in binary judgments under controlled reading conditions. Agreement does not establish that those judgments were correct, and the study does not validate qualitative cine 4D CT for clinical decision-making. Phenotype assignments should be interpreted with the clinical findings and other investigations.
